The researchers conducted the first comprehensive evaluation of emerging materials and manufacturing technologies for fully non-metallic gas turbine engines.
Fused deposition modeling was used to fabricate polymer matrix composite components, while binder jet printing was used to create ceramic matrix composite parts.
Reducing porosity and optimizing mechanical properties were key challenges in the polymer composite fabrication process.
Optimizing the powder composition and infiltration process was critical for increasing the density of the ceramic matrix composites.
The engine systems analysis showed the advanced materials and manufacturing processes could reduce engine weight by 15% and fuel burn by 5%, with an 8.3% reduction in NOx emissions.
The fused deposition modeling for polymer matrix composites was at TRL 4, while the binder jet process for ceramic matrix composites was at TRL 3.
The researchers fabricated inlet guide vanes, compressor blades, acoustic liners, and turbine nozzle segments using the polymer and ceramic matrix composites.
Next steps included optimizing the powder composition, exploring alternate densification approaches, investigating fiber coatings, and reducing porosity in the polymer composites.
The researchers used NPSS, FLOPS, and WATE modeling tools to assess the performance, weight, and fuel burn impacts of the advanced technologies.
Chopped fiber reinforcement increased the modulus of the polymer matrix composites by 40% and the strength by 20%.
Successive infiltrations increased the density of the ceramic matrix composites by 30% by optimizing the powder composition.
The first CMC turbine engine components fabricated by additive manufacturing included nozzle segments and cooled doublet nozzle sections.
The researchers incorporated 20% chopped SiC fibers in the SiC/SiC ceramic matrix composites.
Bimodal powder size distributions and adding SiC powder to the infiltrant improved the packing and infiltration of the ceramic matrix composites.
Reducing the layer thickness and optimizing processing temperature and speed were identified as ways to further improve the properties of the polymer composites.
